consultation_record.consultation_abstract: Elderly male admitted with 'melena for over 1 month.' EGD findings: 1. Gastric cancer; 2. Chronic atrophic gastritis (Kimura-Takemoto C-2). Pathology: (Gastric angle) Adenocarcinoma, moderately to poorly differentiated. (Gastric antrum) Consistent with intramucosal adenocarcinoma, moderately differentiated. H. pylori staining: Negative (-). IHC: HER2 (2+), Claudin 18.2 (+, 2+~3+ in ~80% of cells). Colonoscopy: Endoscopic resection of colorectal polyps (EMR/CSP). Pathology: (Ascending colon 1-2, hepatic flexure 1-3, splenic flexure, descending colon, rectum 1-2) Low-grade tubular adenomas (9 total). Requesting consultation for further management.
consultation_record.consultation_advice: History reviewed. Physical examination: No significant positive findings. Assessment: 1. Gastric adenocarcinoma; 2. Other diagnoses as per referring service. Recommendation: Gastric cancer diagnosis confirmed with surgical indication. Transfer to Colorectal Surgery Service for preoperative evaluation and definitive surgical management.

first_record.description: 1. Elderly male presenting with melena for over 1 month, formed stools, frequency 1-2/day, associated with mid-lower abdominal pain and retrosternal chest pain, non-radiating. Admitted for systematic evaluation. 2. Past medical history: Hypertension x3 years (max BP 160/95 mmHg), on Sacubitril/Valsartan and Amlodipine; Coronary Artery Disease x1 year, on Isosorbide Mononitrate and Nicorandil. Denies COPD, hyperlipidemia, chronic infectious diseases, major trauma, surgery, transfusion, or drug/food allergies. Immunization history unknown. 3. Physical exam: Anemic appearance, pale conjunctiva. Lungs clear to auscultation bilaterally. Regular heart rhythm, no murmurs. Abdomen soft, mild tenderness in mid-lower quadrants, no rebound. 4. Ancillary studies: Chest CT (outside): Bilateral pulmonary nodules, larger nodule in left upper lobe warrants short-interval follow-up or further evaluation; bilateral pulmonary fibrosis, focal emphysema in right upper lobe.
first_record.diagnostic_basis: 1. Elderly male with chief complaint of melena >1 month. 2. PMH: Hypertension, CAD on guideline-directed medical therapy. 3. Physical: Anemic appearance, mild mid-lower abdominal tenderness. 4. Imaging: Bilateral pulmonary nodules, fibrotic changes, focal emphysema.
first_record.differential_diagnosis: 1. Peptic Ulcer Disease: Typically presents with chronic, episodic, rhythmic epigastric pain relieved by food or antacids. EGD indicated for definitive diagnosis. 2. Gastric Cancer: Elderly male with melena raises concern for malignancy; may present with abdominal pain, weight loss, elevated tumor markers. EGD with biopsy is diagnostic gold standard.
first_record.plan: 1. Internal medicine nursing protocol, Level I nursing care, low-sodium low-fat diet. 2. Order labs: CBC with differential, reticulocyte count, folate, vitamin B12, cardiac troponin I, serum iron, ferritin, GI tumor markers (CEA/CA19-9), H. pylori serology, coagulation panel; diagnostic studies: EGD, colonoscopy. 3. Initiate medical therapy: PPI for gastric protection, GI motility agents, cardioprotective medications. 4. Request attending physician guidance for next steps.

other_records.record_content: Elderly male admitted with melena >1 month. EGD: 1. Gastric cancer; 2. Chronic atrophic gastritis (C-2). Pathology: (Gastric angle) Adenocarcinoma, mod-poor diff; (Gastric antrum) Intramucosal adenocarcinoma, mod diff. H. pylori: Negative. IHC: HER2 (2+), Claudin 18.2 (+, 2+~3+ ~80%). Colonoscopy: Endoscopic polypectomy (EMR/CSP) of 9 polyps. Pathology: Low-grade tubular adenomas. Colorectal Surgery consult: Diagnosis confirmed, surgical indication present. Recommendation: Transfer to Colorectal Surgery for operative evaluation. Plan executed after discussion with patient/family.

Transfer Note: Patient admitted 07-19 to Gastroenterology, now transferring to Colorectal Surgery. Admission: Elderly male, melena >1 month. PMH: HTN, CAD on GDMT. Physical: Anemic appearance, soft abdomen, mild mid-lower tenderness. Labs: Hb 98 g/L, ferritin 9.68 ng/mL, iron 5.46 μmol/L, CEA 5.47 ng/mL. ECG: Sinus rhythm, counterclockwise rotation, T-wave changes. EGD/Colonoscopy performed with polypectomy. Pathology: Gastric adenocarcinoma (mod-poor diff), Claudin 18.2 high expression. CT chest/abdomen/pelvis: Pulmonary nodules, hepatic/renal cysts, right renal calculus. Current: No abdominal pain, no hematemesis/melena, tolerating diet. Physical stable. Assessment: 1. Gastric cancer 2. Colonic polyps (s/p resection) 3. Hepatic/renal cysts 4. Right renal calculus 5. HTN Stage 2 6. CAD 7. Pulmonary nodules 8. Chronic atrophic gastritis 9. Anemia. Reason for transfer: Definitive surgical management of gastric cancer. Precautions: 1. Monitor cardiac function 2. Continue anemia correction.

Transfer-In Note: Reviewed transfer documentation, history, and physical. Current status: No abdominal pain, no GI bleeding symptoms, no dysphagia. Physical: Anemic appearance, cardiopulmonary exam unremarkable, abdomen soft/nontender, no hepatosplenomegaly, normal bowel sounds, no edema. Assessment consistent with transfer note. Plan: Proceed with surgical management of gastric malignancy.

Preoperative Discussion Summary: Patient: 70M, admitted for melena. Workup: EGD/colonoscopy with pathology-confirmed gastric adenocarcinoma (mod-poor diff), Claudin 18.2 (+80%), HER2 (2+). CT: No distant metastases. Cardiac evaluation: Stable CAD, diastolic dysfunction on echo, no acute ischemia. Surgical indication: Confirmed gastric cancer, resectable, no absolute contraindications. Planned procedure: Laparoscopic radical gastrectomy with D2 lymphadenectomy. Anesthesia: General endotracheal. Risks discussed: Anastomotic leak, bleeding, infection, DVT/PE, cardiac events, mortality. Patient/family consented. Preoperative preparation: NPO, antibiotic prophylaxis, blood products crossmatched (4U PRBCs), VTE prophylaxis. Special considerations: 1. Cardiac monitoring 2. Continued anemia management. Surgeon pre-op assessment: Patient evaluated, indications confirmed, proceeding with surgery.

Postoperative Note (POD#0): Procedure completed 2025-07-28 16:15. Intraoperative findings: No ascites, liver/peritoneum/small bowel/spleen unremarkable. Tumor located at gastric angle, not penetrating serosa, no palpable lymphadenopathy. Procedure performed: Laparoscopic distal gastrectomy with gastrojejunostomy and Braun anastomosis. Postoperative plan: Cardiac monitoring, supplemental oxygen, nebulizer therapy, PPI, nutritional support, monitor surgical drains. Family notified of procedure details. Morning labs: Inflammatory markers, metabolic panel.

exit_record.treatment: Admission workup: CT chest/abdomen/pelvis (2025-07-22): Pulmonary nodules (follow-up recommended), fibrotic changes, focal emphysema, pleural thickening, hepatic/renal cysts, right renal calculus, pelvic fluid, intraluminal densities (clinical correlation advised). EGD: 1. Gastric cancer; 2. Chronic atrophic gastritis (C-2). Colonoscopy with endoscopic polypectomy (EMR/CSP). After preoperative optimization, underwent laparoscopic distal gastrectomy with gastrojejunostomy and Braun anastomosis (2025-07-28). Final pathology: Tumor location: Gastric antrum, lesser curvature. Size: Two lesions; larger 2.2x1.4 cm, thickness 0.4 cm; smaller 0.8x0.5 cm, thickness 0.2 cm. Morphology: Localized ulcerative type. Histology: Tubular adenocarcinoma, moderately to poorly differentiated. Depth of invasion: Both T1a (larger: muscularis mucosae; smaller: lamina propria). No perforation, no obstruction. No definite lymphovascular invasion. No perineural invasion. Tumor budding: Grade 3. Margins: Negative; larger lesion: proximal 3.2 cm, distal 5.7 cm; smaller: proximal 4.3 cm, distal 3.1 cm. Lymph nodes: Groups 3 (8), 4 (7), 5 (3), 6 (4), 12A (2) – all negative for metastasis. Omentum: Fibroadipose tissue, no tumor. pTNM stage: pT1a N0 Mx. IHC: Claudin 18.2 (2+~3+, ~80%), Syn (-), HER2 (1+), BRAF (-); MMR proteins intact (MLH1/MSH6/PMS2/MSH2 +). Postoperative course: IV fluids, antibiotics, nutritional support. Recovery uncomplicated. Discharged in stable condition.

image_reports.diagnosis:
1. Gastric adenocarcinoma;
2. Chronic atrophic gastritis (Kimura-Takemoto classification C-2).
image_reports.findings: EGD findings: Esophagus: Mucosa smooth, pink, vascular pattern visible, good peristalsis, no abnormalities on NBI. GE junction: Z-line at 40 cm from incisors, well-defined, mucosa smooth, no stricture, normal opening/closure. Gastric fundus/body: Turbid mucus pool, moderate volume. Mucosa smooth, regular arrangement of collecting venules (RAC) pattern lost, rugal folds intact, no ulceration/erosion. Gastric angle/antrum: Arcuate configuration, mucosal erythema, no ulceration/erosion. Gastric angle: ~1.0 cm deep ulcer with nodular raised margins, yellow-white exudate, friable with contact bleeding, ill-defined borders on NBI; 3 biopsies obtained. Gastric antrum (lesser curvature, anterior wall): Rough, erythematous mucosa; 2 biopsies obtained from anterior wall. Pylorus: Round, smooth, normal opening/closure. Duodenum: Bulb, descending portion, and ampulla unremarkable.

image_reports.diagnosis:
Bowel preparation: Boston Bowel Preparation Scale = 8
Endoscopic resection of colorectal polyps (EMR/CSP technique).
image_reports.findings: Colonoscopy findings: Standard prep, left lateral decubitus position. Scope advanced to terminal ileum (70 cm), mucosa smooth. Withdrawal examination: Significant fecal residue in lumen. Findings: Ascending colon, hepatic flexure, splenic flexure, descending colon, rectum: 9 flat/pedunculated polyps, 0.4-0.8 cm diameter, erythematous surface with visible microvasculature. Larger polyps: Submucosal injection with 1:20,000 epinephrine/methylene blue/glycerol-fructose solution, positive lift sign, snare polypectomy with electrocautery, endoclips applied to resection sites. Smaller polyps: Snare polypectomy, endoclips applied. No active bleeding at resection sites. Remainder of colon: Mucosa smooth, vascular pattern intact.

image_reports.diagnosis: Ultrasound-guided right subclavian central venous catheter placement
image_reports.findings: Indication: Central venous access for perioperative management. Procedure: Patient supine. Ultrasound guidance for site selection. Standard sterile prep and draping. Local anesthesia with 2% lidocaine. Under real-time color Doppler guidance, needle advanced into right subclavian vein avoiding vascular structures. Guidewire inserted, tract dilated, dual-lumen central venous catheter advanced to 16 cm depth. Guidewire removed, catheter secured and dressed.

operations.intra_diagnosis: 1. Gastric Malignancy 2. Essential Hypertension, Stage 2, Very High Risk 3. Coronary Artery Disease 4. Bilateral Pulmonary Nodules
operations.op_name: Laparoscopic Distal Gastrectomy with Gastrojejunostomy and Braun Anastomosis
operations.pre_diagnosis: 1. Gastric Malignancy 2. Essential Hypertension, Stage 2, Very High Risk 3. Coronary Artery Disease 4. Bilateral Pulmonary Nodules
operations.process: After induction of general endotracheal anesthesia, patient positioned supine with legs split. Standard sterile prep and draping. Foley catheter placed. Pneumoperitoneum established. Five-port laparoscopic technique: Observation port and operating ports placed. Exploration: No ascites. Liver, peritoneum, small bowel, spleen unremarkable. Tumor identified at gastric angle, not penetrating serosa, no palpable perigastric lymphadenopathy. Decision: Proceed with laparoscopic distal gastrectomy with gastrojejunostomy and Braun anastomosis. Greater omentum mobilized: Flipped cephalad, divided from transverse colon (left-sided start) using ultrasonic shears, entering lesser sac, extended to splenic and hepatic flexures. Greater curvature dissection: Extended to splenic flexure, left gastroepiploic vessels skeletonized at pancreatic tail, ligated at origin, station 4sb lymphadenectomy performed, distal dissection to planned resection margin. Lesser curvature dissection: Right gastroepiploic vessels skeletonized below pylorus, ligated at origin, station 6 lymphadenectomy. Common hepatic artery identified above pancreas, station 8 lymphadenectomy. Right gastric vessels identified along common hepatic artery, ligated at origin, stations 5 and 12a lymphadenectomy. Duodenal bulb mobilized, divided with laparoscopic linear stapler. Anterior pancreatic capsule dissected; left gastric vessels identified along superior pancreatic border, ligated at origin. Gastric lesser curvature: Ultrasonic shears used for layered division, stations 1 and 3 lymphadenectomy performed. Reconstruction: Anvil of circular stapler (29mm) placed ~15cm distal to ligament of Treitz; side-to-side gastrojejunostomy performed ~5cm proximal to tumor. Gastric transection ~4cm proximal to tumor with linear stapler; staple lines and anastomosis reinforced with absorbable sutures. Braun enteroenterostomy: Side-to-side anastomosis between afferent and efferent jejunal limbs ~30cm and ~10cm from gastrojejunostomy, respectively; anastomosis and staple lines reinforced with seromuscular sutures. Irrigation and hemostasis: Surgical field irrigated, meticulous hemostasis confirmed, instrument/sponge count correct. Drains placed: One drain below liver/adjacent to duodenal stump, one drain in splenic bed. Procedure uneventful, minimal blood loss. Transfused: 4 units PRBCs, 200ml FFP. Anesthesia: Adequate. Patient transferred to PACU. Specimens sent to pathology.

Second lesion: 4.3 cm from proximal margin, 3.1 cm from distal margin, measuring 0.8 x 0.5 cm, gray-white firm cut surface, maximum thickness 0.2 cm, confined to mucosal layer; lesions separated by 1 cm. Attached greater omentum: 30 x 22 cm, thickness 0.3-0.7 cm, yellow-gray, soft, no palpable nodules or lymph nodes.
Lymph node dissection:
  - Station 3 (lesser curvature): 8 nodes, largest 1.6 cm, gray-white, soft.
  - Station 4 (greater curvature): 7 nodes, largest 1.1 cm, gray-white, soft.
  - Station 5 (suprapyloric): 3 nodes, largest 1.3 cm, gray-white, soft.
  - Station 6 (infrapyloric): 4 nodes, largest 0.5 cm, gray-white, soft.
  - Station 12A (hepatic artery): 2 nodes, largest 0.8 cm, gray-white, soft.
